title: Deriving the Wave Equation
eyebrow: Goosethropic Physics · Waves · computed in Rust via WebAssembly
lede: There is nothing wavy in the ingredients: beads, string, Newton. Pluck the chain, then use the four steps to dissect one bead at any frozen instant — its two tension pulls, and the single approximation the whole derivation stands on, measured live. Raise the bead count to take the limit yourself.

steps.title: 1 · One bead, Newton's law
steps.html:
The highlighted bead has mass m = μ·Δx — its share of the string. Newton:

m·ÿᵢ = Fᵢ

Everything that follows is bookkeeping on Fᵢ. Pause anywhere — the dissector below the chain shows this bead magnified at the frozen instant.

steps.title: 2 · The two tension pulls
steps.html:
Only the two string segments touch the bead. Each pulls with tension T along itself (gold, in the dissector). The true transverse part of each pull is T·sin θ (solid); the derivation instead uses the slope, T·tan θ = T·Δy/Δx (dashed). At honest amplitudes you cannot tell them apart — the error readout says by how little. Now drag the amplitude slider up and watch the dashed and solid arrows split: that is the small-angle approximation failing, measured.

Fᵢ ≈ T·[(yᵢ₊₁ − yᵢ)/Δx − (yᵢ − yᵢ₋₁)/Δx]

steps.title: 3 · The bracket is curvature
steps.html:
ÿᵢ = (T/μ)·(yᵢ₊₁ − 2yᵢ + yᵢ₋₁)/Δx²

The second difference is sampled curvature — and the red arrow at the dissected bead is exactly it: peaks accelerate down, valleys up, straight stretches feel nothing. Watch the arrow vanish whenever the chain runs locally straight through the bead.

steps.title: 4 · Send Δx → 0
steps.html:
∂²y/∂t² = c²·∂²y/∂x², c = √(T/μ)

Now take the limit yourself: raise the bead slider and watch pluck speed vs c climb toward 100%. One honest wrinkle stays: the chain's shortest waves travel at 4/τ ≈ 64% of c no matter how many beads — what the limit fixes is every wave a smooth pluck contains. The wave equation is Newton with the bookkeeping finished.

tryThis: Freeze mid-flight, set amplitude ×2.4, and read the tan-for-sin error — then ask: at what error would YOU stop trusting the derivation?
Pluck dead centre and step to 3: which bead never feels a net pull, and why?
Set N = 5 and play: the trailing wiggles are dispersion — the waves the limit has not yet rescued.
Watch the pluck split into two half-height travellers — d'Alembert's y = f(x−ct) + g(x+ct) in the flesh — and flip upside down at each wall.
